transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sarah Lee (NexaHead of Data), Dr. Alan Park (CTO), Priya Singh (DevOps), Carlos Mendes (ML Eng), Tom Reed (Procurement)
---
Summary (auto): weekly checkin, onboarding items, access blockers, benchmark request, security doc share, schedule perf run
---
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check, can you see my screen?
00:08 Sarah: Yep, we can see it. Thanks Maya. Good to have you.
:15 Maya: Cool. So agenda - quick onboarding status, access and VPC, results from the small run we did last week, tuning notes, then next steps. Anything to add?
00:30 Dr. Park: No, that covers it. Tom just wants to make sure procurement timeline is still okay.
00:36 Tom: Yeah, nothing urgent, just heads up on contracting.
00:42 Liam: I'll jump in on the perf stuff, Maya will handle the security docs.
00:47 Maya: Great. Okay first item - onboarding. Priya, where are we on peering?
00:55 Priya: We kicked off with our network team; the peering request is in with infra, they said 2-3 business days. I did hit one snag with route tables, some of the CIDR ranges overlap with an older VPC we have, so we're cleaning that up. Should be resolved by Monday.
01:15 Maya: Ok that aligns with what we saw. In the meantime we can set up a temporary SSH bastion to give you access to the test endpoints. Liam, did you already put the SSH keys?
01:24 Liam: Yeah I provisioned a bastion host in the dev account; access keys were emailed to Carlos, though looks like some of the lines in the email got wrapped — a bit messy in the transcription, but Carlos confirm you have the key?
01:36 Carlos: I have the key, but I couldn't ssh earlier because the security group was missing the egress rule to the redwood subnet. Priya corrected that yesterday and I could connect.
01:45 Maya: Perfect. So access is nominally good for Carlos. Priya, once peering is done we'll switch to the full test flow and revoke the temporary bastion.
01:58 Priya: Sounds good. We'll update the ticket.
02:05 Maya: Next, SSO. Sarah, you were going to test the SAML integration?
02:12 Sarah: Yes, we tried the SAML flow in your staging control plane. We got to the assertion but the NameID mapping was off, Redwood's attribute mapping expects 'email' and ours is sending 'userPrincipalName'. I think that's a small mapping change on our IdP side. We'll send our SAML metadata.
02:31 Maya: We can accept userPrincipalName - Liam, is that quick to adjust?
02:35 Liam: Yeah it's just a mapping table, I can add an alias for NameID -> email/userPN. Should be trivial.
02:42 Sarah: We'll push the metadata by tomorrow.
02:44 Maya: Great. Ok now the results from the small run — Liam?
02:50 Liam: Sure, quick context, last week we ran a 100-sample throughput/latency test against the hosted endpoint and a lightweight dedicated config. We saw median latency ~220ms on hosted (our small instance) for short prompts and about 410ms for longer 1k-token-ish prompts; dedicated was lower at about 180ms median for the same set, but cost delta is about 2.3x. The tradeoff math still holds: dedicated for steady high throughput, hosted for burst. There were a few anomalies in the logs - rapid spikes during a specific prompt that had heavy retrievals.
03:30 Carlos: On the anomalies, I think those prompts hit our external DB for context retrieval which added network time; the Redwood test used the same retrieval call pattern as our prod. We need to separate network lookups from model latency in the bench.
03:45 Liam: Good call. We'll run an isolated bench that mocks retrieval latency locally.
03:50 Dr. Park: Also, curious about batching and quantization—what's the recommended config for our workload (short chat + occasional long docs)?
03:58 Liam: For mixed workloads, start with dynamic batching with a 20ms micro-batch window and a target batch size of 8 for your traffic shape. For long-doc generation, enable kv-cache affinity on dedicated nodes and consider int8 quantization on models that are validated — we have a QC profile for the 7b and 13b family. That said, quantization improved cost ~35% in our tests but some responses degrade on rare cases, so we recommend evals on your prompt set.
04:32 Carlos: Are those QC profiles in the doc you sent? I couldn't find the 13b int8 notes.
04:38 Maya: I'll resend the quantization profiles in the security + ops packet. Liam, please point Carlos to the 13b int8 section.
04:46 Liam: Will do. Also note, small transcription glitch from our auto notes - sometimes KV cache becomes 'KV cash' in the transcript, so ignore that.
04:53 (laughter)
04:55 Sarah: Ha, yeah that shows up. Ok on tuning — we want to run a 1k prompt test next week. The ask is 95th percentile latency and quality regression checks vs a golden set. Can you do both?
05:07 Liam: Yep, we can run latency experiments and our eval harness can compute quality deltas against your golden responses. We'll need the 1k prompts and golden responses from Carlos and the expected pass thresholds.
05:20 Carlos: I can hand over the 1k prompts, but a heads-up: there are PII-like placeholders in a few prompts, so I will sanitize and send the version. Expect that by Monday.
05:30 Sarah: Also security asks: we need to see audit logs for model invocations, and confirm logs don't include raw customer data in the control plane.
05:39 Maya: Correct — Redwood's private deployment keeps logs in your VPC by default in the private plane. For hosted we redact by default and provide audit logs in the console; we'll share the exact retention and fields in the doc pack.
05:51 Tom: On procurement, any differences in billing for dedicated vs hosted for the POC period? We want to avoid surprise overages.
05:58 Maya: For the POC we cap usage at the agreed committed amount; any overages are notified and must be approved. We'll add a billing guardrail for your account.
06:08 Tom: Good.
06:10 Liam: Quick note on the benchmark: to measure pure model latency we'll provide a mode that removes retrieval and network; then we can reintroduce retrieval to show total end-to-end. That should satisfy Carlos' ask.
06:22 Carlos: Perfect. Also, I saw a drop in token throughput when quantization flag was on for one model — there might be a mismatch in the kernel selection path. Is that expected?
06:33 Liam: There are a couple of reasons: on some GPU/driver combinations quantized kernels can be less optimized than FP16. We'll run kernel selection traces during the perf run and share logs. If needed we can pin a different kernel or model variant.
06:47 Dr. Park: What's the timeline for the performance run?
06:50 Maya: We suggested week of 4/19 based on everyone's availability. Carlos and Liam can pick a slot and Marcos — sorry, I mean Priya — will confirm peering is done by then.
07:02 Priya: I'll push for peering to be complete by Monday, 4/19. If there's a slip I'll notify Maya.
07:08 Sarah: Ok. A couple of compliance questions — does Redwood support bringing your own KMS for key management in private?
07:16 Maya: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS, and we can do HSM integrations for enterprise. We'll include the KMS options in the doc pack.
07:27 Sarah: Also need SOC2 type II evidence and pen test summary.
07:31 Maya: I'll attach SOC2 and our latest pen test summary; if you need the full report we can set an NDA.
07:37 Tom: NDA is fine, procurement will initiate.
07:40 Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
07:43 Carlos: Minor: for the eval harness, can we get the scoring metrics config (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim thresholds)? I didn't see that in the shared sheet.
07:51 Liam: We have a default config; I'll attach the config file and we can tune thresholds to your golden set.
07:56 Carlos: Thanks.
07:58 Maya: Ok let's recap action items. Maya to send security pack and quant profiles by EOD 4/15; Priya to confirm VPC peering by 4/19; Carlos to deliver sanitized 1k prompts by 4/18; Liam to schedule and run the latency+eval harness week of 4/19 and share logs by 4/22. Sarah will provide SAML metadata by 4/15.
08:30 Sarah: That sounds right.
08:33 Tom: Procurement will start NDA and put procurement items in motion.
08:36 Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone for time. We'll follow up in Slack and link the benchmark calendar invite.
08:43 Dr. Park: Thanks all. Bye.
08:45 End call.
---
Notes on transcript quality: automated timestamps approximate, speaker labels mostly correct though sometimes 'Marcos' vs 'Priya' mishearings occurred. Occasional filler words and ASR mistakes (KV cash, userPN vs userPrincipalName) present.
